message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the maximum speed allowed.
• Drivers may drive at a speed that is “reasonable and prudent” for conditions, even if below the posted limit. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning or changing lanes. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red = stop; Green = go; Yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for violations such as illegal parking or obstruction. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must be current and displayed.
• Minimum liability insurance required. | | **Roadway Safety** | • Use of headlights between sunset and sunrise.
• No driving in hazardous weather without proper precautions. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) – the statutory source for all traffic laws. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – provides handbooks, forms, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement and public safety resources. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Speed cameras and radar guns are used on major highways. - Police may issue citations for seat‑belt violations, cell‑phone use, and DUI. - Repeat offenders may face increased penalties, license suspension, or mandatory education programs. **Recent Updates (2024)** - Texas has introduced stricter penalties for texting while driving. - New regulations on electric vehicle charging stations and their impact on roadways. - Updated guidelines for autonomous vehicle testing on public roads. If you need more specific details—such as the exact wording of a statute, recent case law, or how a particular rule applies to a unique situation—just let me know!
